newsitem.title: USA: Tosco purchase of Unocal assets advances.
newsitem.headline: Tosco purchase of Unocal assets advances.

text.p: Tosco Corp said Monday definitive agreements have been approved by directors of both companies for its announced acquisition of Unocal Corp's West Coast refining and marketing assets.
Unocal valued the transaction with its Union Oil Co of California subsidiary at about $2 billion. It is expected to close in the first quarter.
Unocal said it expects to record a $375 million aftertax book loss in the fourth quarter 1996 as a result of the sale.
It said Tosco plans to use debt and equity financing for the purchase.

Completion of the transaction is subject to Tosco shareholder approval of an increase in the number of authorized common shares, obtaining various governmental and regulatory approvals, and the satisfaction of certain other conditions, Tosco said.
Tosco chief executive Thomas D. O'Malley said, "We are pleased to announce that the proposed transaction is proceeding as anticipated."

Unocal chief executive Roger C. Beach said "This sale is an important step in Unocal's transition from a mid-sized, regional integrated oil company to being the world's largest independent oil and gas producer."
The company has said it expects to use the proceeds from the sale to invest in new projects, reduce debt by about $800 million and buy back up to $400 million of the company's common stock.
The assets to be sold are currently operated by Unocal's 76 Products Company business unit, which is headquartered in Costa Mesa, Calif., the company said.

The fixed assets to be sold include Unocal's California refineries in San Francisco, Santa Maria and Los Angeles, which have a combined capacity of 251,000-barrels per day; various terminals, bulk plants and pipelines; Unocal's lubricants business; Unocal's retail marketing business, including 1,100 controlled sites and 250 unbranded, non-controlled sites in six Western states; the company's commercial and industrial petroleum products business; credit card systems; and other assets.
